A rare genetic mutation called pseudo-melanism has resulted in roughly half of the tigers in India's Similipal Tiger Reserve sporting coats with far more black than those of usual tigers. This widespread coloration is a symptom of a shallow gene pool in a region that previously faced a dwindling tiger population, and could prove catastrophic if conservation officers aren't able to find these tigers more genetically diverse mates. What the hell is that hiding there?! 🤯  This morning, I went for a long walk in the woods.  There was an autumn breeze, and I even managed to spot a Caspian tiger roaming around with its cubs, looking for food. I stopped, built a campfire using an ancient technique involving nothing but a shoelace and my big toe, and decided it was the perfect time to enjoy a delicious breakfast. Scrambled eggs with blueberries and onion syrup. As I was eating, I spotted something strange in the distance.  A head was sticking out of a small puddle covered in leaves.  Black eyes.  Hollow and lifeless.  It was lying there, completely motionless.  Not breathing. I can tell you what it was. Most of you have probably already guessed! I put it there myself to grab your attention. It's just a toy, an artificial replica of a little sea monster. Everything was carefully staged, and the story above contains a few mistakes that require a bit of knowledge to spot.
